- R1-1 — resolved (prior confirmed Blocking, iteration 1; resolution recorded here, not a new rejection). All nine completed scouts independently assess the missing progress/latency contract fixed. Present evidence verified in settled-input.md:120, :167 and :262: the root, receipt and invitation refinements retain the 5,000ms safety tick and 100-candidate drive cap, require immediate successful continuation and fair stable finite high-water cursors independent of native wakes, and bound durable pending-warning discovery by 5,000ms + (2*ceil(N/100)+2)*Q under explicit healthy-daemon, successful bounded-storage/scheduling and finite-snapshot assumptions. New arrivals cannot restart or starve the current snapshot; restart resumes or reconstructs discovery. ht-0lo.1.2 description/acceptance (:717/:718) and ht-0lo.2.2 (:649/:650) require early fake-clock fixtures with at least 250 candidates in EACH class, blocked native wakes, mixed future/due rows, continuing arrivals and restart, asserting the formula and no starvation. ht-0lo.1.3 (:405/:406) requires historical upgrade over multiple bounded batches. This resolves the design dependency without promising bounded native submission, outages, repeated errors or unbounded overload; implementation and test execution remain future work.
- R1-4 — resolved (prior confirmed Blocking, iteration 1; resolution recorded here, not a new rejection). All nine completed scouts independently assess the ordinary-send compatibility boundary fixed. Present evidence verified in settled-input.md:122, :169 and :217: messages.send_time_receipts_v1 is advertised only with active canonical send-time projection and ordinary-send handlers; modern clients require it before every new ACK-required ordinary send or handoff durable/native effect, including all CLI and service-capable sends promising the contract. Absent/refused discovery produces explicit unsupported-daemon refusal with no silent fallback. Old-client/upgraded-daemon canonical semantics, lazy/human exemptions, immutable completed historical replay and refusal before additional pending historical retry effects are explicit. ht-0lo.1.1 description/acceptance (:763/:764) owns capability enforcement and new-client/old-daemon, old-client/new-daemon, current unbound and exemption fixtures. ht-0lo.3.2 (:443/:444) consumes the capability and requires refusal before staging/launch. This supplies the enforceable semantic boundary previously missing; implementation and fixture execution remain future work.
